summary: Elevated 502/503 error floor on streaming chat route during priority-handshake stampede for NexaHealth (dedicated)
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-12 08:14 UTC we observed a sustained elevation in 502/503 responses on the /v1/chat/streaming endpoint for NexaHealth's dedicated tenancy. Impact: customer-facing failed requests for streaming chat sessions (intermittent 5xx, ~12-18% error-rate for the tenant), degraded latency for successful sessions, and visible client reconnect churn. Environment: prod - dedicated fleet in us-west-2, tenant pinned to redwood-open-7b-quant-v2. Steps to reproduce: 1) Initiate ~300 concurrent streaming connections that immediately start an auth/handshake then send a short transcript; 2) Observe connection establishment / TLS handshake wave; 3) Watch 502/503s and streaming session resets escalate after ~30s. Observed around tenant priority routing changes and a burst of hedged retries from the edge. Logs & dashboards: refer to apigw/error_rate (2026-03-12 08:10-09:00), runtime-proxy/handshake_metrics, and kvcache/lock_counts. Customer report: NexaHealth observed client SDK reconnect loop and requested immediate mitigation.
investigation_notes: 08:18 UTC - Alert from SLO that NexaHealth streaming error rate crossed 10% (page oncall)
Initial hypothesis: ephemeral TLS/session cache exhaustion at api-gateway combined with upstream runtime preemption during priority-handshake fan-in
apigw logs show transient TLS handshake stalls (increase in handshake_time p95 from 12ms -> 480ms) coincident with keepalive drop events
runtime-proxy metrics show surge in new upstream connections and concurrent prefetched KV cache locks (kvcache_lock_wait_count spike)
Observed many hedged retries from edge: client-side retries + apigw hedged request policy amplified upstream fanout
NVML / GPU metrics: no immediate GPU OOMs, but runtime processes reported increased page-faults and occasional SIGTERM from scheduler while preempting ephemeral workers
Heap/FD counts on runtime showed accept-queue backlog growth and intermittent EADDRNOTAVAIL for ephemeral proxies
Correlated with a priority routing change at 08:12 UTC (canary -> weight shift) in route config for NexaHealth (see linked_issues)
Reproduced locally in staging by replaying handshake pattern and observed same accept-queue spike and kvcache lock contention
comments: Maya Chen (Support) - 2026-03-12 08:25: Customer reports SDK reconnect loop and many clients failing to get initial response. Asked SRE to triage immediately.
Evelyn Hart (SRE) - 2026-03-12 08:35: Investigating apigw handshake latency and upstream preemptions. Pulling runtime-proxy traces and NVML logs.
Arjun Patel (Serving Eng) - 2026-03-12 09:02: Not seeing OOMs but runtime shows preemption during heavy accept-queue growth. Possible link to hedged retry amplification from edge.

Maya Chen (Support) - 2026-03-12 09:18: Relay to NexaHealth minimal mitigation steps: reduce client retry aggressiveness and enable SDK jittering. Customer requested temporary route pin to a stable variant.
Evelyn Hart (SRE) - 2026-03-12 09:40: Temporarily increased apigw keepalive pool size and disabled hedged retries for the affected route; error-rate dropped to ~3% after change.
Product Ops - 2026-03-13 11:05: Noted the priority route weight shift that coincided with event; scheduling follow-up to review rollout safeguards for priority changes.
NexaHealth (customer) - 2026-03-13 12:30: Confirmed improved stability after mitigation but would like permanent fix to avoid future manual mitigations.
resolution_notes: Mitigation applied: disabled hedged retries at edge for the affected route, increased API gateway keepalive pool, and temporarily pinned NexaHealth to a stable variant with a conservative prefetch policy. Post-mitigation monitoring showed error-rate reduced from ~15% -> 2.8% within 18 minutes. Follow-ups: engineering to (1) add guardrails to route weight rollouts (automated slow ramp + preflight handshake tests), (2) implement apigw TLS/session-cache autoshrink detection and graceful backpressure, (3) enhance hedged-retry amplification protection (circuit-break on upstream accept-queue growth). Customer success will coordinate a post-incident RCA call with NexaHealth. Assigned follow-up tickets: INT-2026-014 (deploy route-rollout preflight), SUP-472901 (related connection thrash incident).
